ai.description: *Pseudoxenodon macrops* reaches 100 cm. It is olive-brown with dark, yellow-edged vertebral blotches and a distinct neck hood. It features a prominent black stripe behind each large eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Pseudoxenodon macrops* is the presence of a distinct, dark V-shaped mark on the nape, contrasting with its variable dorsal pattern.
ai.habitat: This species inhabits moist, dense evergreen and broadleaf forests in the Himalayan foothills and Northeast India, typically at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Large-eyed False Cobra flattens its neck to mimic a cobra and may strike with a closed mouth to deter potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pseudoxenodon macrops* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with eggs deposited in moist, sheltered sites.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Pseudoxenodon macrops* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas and Northeast India, typically inhabiting moist forests at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
